fact: Guinea's president signed a decree on 19 August 2026 applying article 1003 of the Civil Code on electronic signature, giving an electronic signature the same probative force as a paper writing, covering public, private and person-to-person acts, and taking effect on signature.
system: Decree applying article 1003 of the Civil Code on electronic signature

fact: The decree of 19 August 2026 requires every electronic-certification service provider to be approved by the competent authority, names the national digital agency ANDE as that authority for approval, control and audit, and refers technical standards to a joint order of the telecommunications and justice ministries; it reports no provider approved.
system: Decree applying article 1003 of the Civil Code on electronic signature

fact: Law L/2016/035/AN of 26 July 2016 on electronic transactions was promulgated; ANSSI's summary says it applies to all electronic transactions including online commerce, and covers electronic signature, digital archiving, system certification, consumer information duties, fines and prison terms (the document is a summary of an image-only scan).
system: Loi L/2016/035/AN relative aux transactions electroniques

fact: ANSSI's page states that Decree D/2021/092/PRG/SGG, signed 25 March 2021 under Law L/2016/035/AN of 26 July 2016 on electronic transactions, sets rules for electronic transactions including e-commerce (secure transaction facility, .gn or .com domain, prices in francs), names the ARPT as regulator with sanction powers, and provides fines and penalties (the scan itself is image-only, so this is ANSSI's summary).
system: Décret D/2021/092/PRG/SGG portant sur les transactions électroniques

fact: A government representative said article 1003 of the Civil Code gives strict equivalence between handwritten and electronic signature, per Guineenews.
Guineenews reports an implementing decree fixing the modalities of electronic signature under article 1003 of the Civil Code was adopted on 19 August 2026.
